summary: Scheduled allocator preemptions causing ephemeral KV-cache pressure and sustained p99 throughput degradation for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
During Tellus Analytics' scheduled ingest window (09:00-11:00 PDT) on 2026-03-10 they observed a ~30% sustained drop in p50/p99 throughput on their dedicated capacity pool, with frequent preemptive GPU lease revocations and elevated KV-cache eviction rates. Traffic spike pattern: many short-lived small streams from telemetry ingestion leading to allocator churn.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency increase: p99 up to 2.1s from baseline 700ms for batched text-generation routes.
- Requests falling back to hosted fallback model twice during the window causing extra cost and partial feature degradation.
- No data loss but elevated retries and increased token bill.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: tellus-dedicated-west (reserved GPUs: 8 x A40-equivalents)
- Region: us-west-2
- Routes impacted: /v1/generate (batched), /v1/stream (short-streams)

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) During scheduled ingest (09:00-11:00 PDT) customer ramps from 200->1,200 concurrent short streams (avg lifetime 150-400ms).
2) Cluster allocator begins preempting low-priority leases to satisfy perceived new requests, causing GPU lease revocations and reattachment pauses.
3) KV-cache eviction rate spikes as sessions churn; subsequent warmed batches miss prefix cache and force recompute.
4) Autoscaler shows multiple rapid shrink/grow cycles correlated to the short-lived bursts which amplifies eviction.

Logs / Evidence:
- Serving runtime logs (snippet): "lease-preempt request=0x7f2f alloc=slot-13 -> revoked for tenant=tellus-123 at 2026-03-10T16:07:12Z"
- KV cache monitor: sustained eviction_rate=4200 evict/s (baseline ~120 evict/s) from 09:03-10:15 PDT.
- Autoscaler events: 09:05 scale-down, 09:06 scale-up x2 within 90s, repeated 09:10-09:30.
- Trace link: https://observability.redwood.com/trace/4372c9 (internal)

Initial hypothesis:
- Short-lived stream fanout triggers allocator heuristics that favor immediate allocation over stable batching, causing lease churn and KV-cache thrashing.
- Autoscaler sensitivity combined with slot preemption policy is oscillating under bursty short streams.
- Potential noisy-neighbor behavior from another tenant in the same reserved pool triggering frequent small allocations.

Immediate customer impact mitigation performed by support:
- Temporarily applied tenant-affinity pinning to keep Tellus workloads on a separate set of slots for the remainder of the ingest window (reduced preemptions).
- Throttled low-priority background tenants in the same cluster for 2 hours (mitigated the p99 degradation).

Requested by customer:
- Durable fix to avoid allocator preemptive revocations during scheduled ingest windows.
- Guidance on configuration to reduce KV-cache churn for many short-lived streams.
investigation: 09:20 - Correlated autoscaler events with serving runtime lease logs; pattern shows revocations preceding p99 spikes.
09:35 - Identified a secondary tenant (tenant-id: noisy-501) launching burst of ephemeral streams at same time window. Their allocation behavior matches preemption windows.
10:10 - Reproduced degraded behavior in staging by replaying short-stream workload; observed scale oscillation and high eviction rate.
11:00 - Kernel-level metrics show increased PCIe stalls when multiple leases reattach simultaneously; may amplify latency.
Hypothesis refined: combination of allocator preemption policy + autoscaler sensitivity + KV-cache LRU eviction threshold causes worsened throughput under many short streams.

SRE (Jordan Malik) 2026-03-10 09:40: Confirmed lease revocation events in logs. Suggested immediate tenant-affinity pinning and to check autoscaler smoothing window.
Customer (Priya Raman, Tellus) 2026-03-10 10:02: Thank you — pinning helped but we still saw intermittent fallbacks between 09:50-10:05.
Eng (Ethan Ross) 2026-03-10 11:15: Replayed workload in staging; captured same eviction spike. Opening PR to add hysteresis to allocator preemption logic for sub-1s streams. See PR 4123.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-11 08:30: Applied temporary autoscaler smoothing change on tellus-dedicated-west (increase min-scale-hold to 180s). Observed improved stability during smaller bursts.
SRE (Jordan Malik) 2026-03-12 14:20: Noted residual PCIe stall correlation; scheduling a hardware-metrics deep-dive with infra team for 2026-03-13.

resolution: Workaround applied: tenant-affinity pinning + temporary throttling of co-located background tenants reduced p99 by ~45% for the following ingest window.

Medium-term fix: engineering to land allocator hysteresis & preemption holdback for sub-1s streams (PR 4123) and increase autoscaler smoothing defaults for dedicated pools with known short-stream workloads.

Follow-ups: 1) Runbook entry for customers: recommended pool configuration and recommended client-side batching/backoff patterns. 2) Postmortem to be produced if PR change is rolled to prod. 3) Schedule a dedicated capacity anti-noise policy to isolate noisy tenants at allocation time.
Owner: Ethan Ross (eng) for allocator changes; Jordan Malik (SRE) for autoscaler tuning; Maya Chen (Support) to coordinate customer communications and runbook delivery.
